parole.significato: In the Middle East or southwest Asia: a bribe or tip.
parole.testo: From Turkish bahşiş, from Persian بخشیش (baxšiš, “present; an honorary or pecuniary gratuity; drink-money”) or بخشش (baxšeš), from بخشیدن (baxšidan, “to give, grant, bestow”).

parole.significato: A member of a Sufi Muslim ascetic fraternity of mendicant friars.
parole.testo: From Turkish derviş, from Persian درویش (darviš).
From Modern Turkish dümbek, from Ottoman Turkish دنبك (dümbek), from Persian دنبک (donbak). Doublet of tombak.

parole.significato: A flat tapestry-woven carpet or rug from Turkey or Kurdistan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish kilim, from Persian گلیم (gelim), akin to Aramaic גלימא (galīmā, “blanket, garment, cloth”), both from Ancient Greek κάλυμμα (kálumma, “cover, top, covering”) derived from καλύπτω (kalúptō, “to cover”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to cover”).

parole.significato: A blend of henna and various other ingredients, traditionally used to dye the hair.
parole.testo: From Turkish rastık, from Ottoman Turkish راستق (rastık), itself from Persian راسخت (râsoxt). Apparently ultimately from Persian for "burnt copper"; see Arabic رُوسَخْتَج (rūsaḵtaj) for more.
